chapters.title: Chapter 2: Reading Where India Is in the Cycle

lessons.title: Leading, Coincident, and Lagging Indicators: India's Cycle Dashboard

body.text: No single number tells you where the cycle is. A dashboard does: indicators that move before the economy, with it, and after it, read together and in the right order.

children.text: Chapter 1 ended with an uncomfortable truth: GDP arrives too late to guide investment decisions, and the market turns before the economy does. So what do you actually watch? This lesson sorts India's most useful economic data into three families, shows you when each is released, and flags the traps that make even good data misleading.
Three Families of Indicators

body.caption: How indicators line up against the cycle

cells: Where activity is likely heading over the next few months
Manufacturing and services PMI (especially new orders), the Nifty, bond yield curve, auto sales, bank credit momentum
What activity is doing right now
Index of Industrial Production (IIP), Index of Core Industries, GST collections, power demand, GDP
Confirms a turn that has already happened
Core CPI inflation, unemployment rate, bank gross NPAs, corporate earnings, capacity utilisation

body.text: GDP is coincident by nature but lagging by release. It measures activity in the quarter it covers, but it is published about two months after that quarter ends and revised later. For an investor making decisions today, it behaves like a lagging indicator.

children.text: Leading Indicators
The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI)

markDefs.definition: An index that measures how widespread a change is across respondents, not how big it is. It adds the percentage reporting an increase to half the percentage reporting no change. A reading of 50 means as many firms report improvement as deterioration.

children.text: The PMI is the most watched leading indicator in India because it is fast, forward looking, and rarely revised. Every month, S&P Global surveys purchasing managers at several hundred Indian manufacturing and services companies, and publishes the results under the HSBC India PMI name. Each question simply asks whether something is higher, the same, or lower than last month, and the answers are turned into a
diffusion index

body.caption: A reading above 50 means more firms report improvement than deterioration; below 50 means the reverse
Headline manufacturing PMI: New Orders, Output, Employment, Suppliers' Delivery Times (inverted), Stocks of Purchases

children.text: Two things make the PMI powerful for cycle watchers. First, the new orders component carries the largest weight and genuinely leads, because orders placed today become production next month. Second, the PMI measures breadth and direction, which is exactly what the market trades. Its weakness is the flip side: it tells you how many firms are improving, not by how much.

body.title: Build a Diffusion Index
body.prompt: In a monthly survey, 34% of manufacturers report higher new orders than last month, 48% report no change, and 18% report lower new orders. What is the New Orders sub-index?
body.explanation: 34 plus half of 48 (which is 24) gives 58. The 18% reporting lower orders do not add anything. A reading of 58 signals that improvement is widespread. Notice that it says nothing about the size of the increase, only that far more firms saw orders rise than fall.

body.title: Calculate the Headline PMI
body.prompt: Using the S&P Global weights, calculate the headline manufacturing PMI from these sub-indices: New Orders 58, Output 56, Employment 51, Suppliers' Delivery Times (already inverted) 52, Stocks of Purchases 50. Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: 0.30 x 58 = 17.4, plus 0.25 x 56 = 14.0, plus 0.20 x 51 = 10.2, plus 0.15 x 52 = 7.8, plus 0.10 x 50 = 5.0. The total is 54.4, a healthy expansion led by orders and output, with hiring lagging behind.

body.title: India manufacturing PMI, January to October 2020

children.text: Compare this chart with Lesson 1.3. The August 2020 PMI of 52.0, the first reading above 50 since the lockdown, was published at the start of September 2020, within days of the record -23.9% GDP print for April to June. The leading indicator was already signalling recovery while the coincident indicator was still reporting catastrophe. By October the PMI hit 58.9, its highest since May 2010.

body.text: Read the PMI as a month-on-month measure. After a collapse, a reading above 50 only means conditions are improving compared to a terrible previous month, not that output is back to normal. The 58.9 reading of October 2020 came while many industries were still producing below pre-Covid levels.

children.text: High-Frequency Activity Data
Beyond the PMI, a handful of monthly and fortnightly numbers give an early read on demand. Some lead slightly, some are closer to coincident, but all arrive far faster than GDP.

Auto sales. Carmakers such as Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors, and Mahindra and Mahindra release monthly sales on the first day of the following month. Two-wheeler and tractor sales are a useful read on rural demand; trucks reflect goods movement and capex.

Bank credit growth. The RBI publishes scheduled commercial bank data fortnightly and sector-wise lending monthly. Accelerating loan growth to industry and consumers usually signals a strengthening cycle.
GST collections and e-way bills. Collections for the previous month are usually made public in the first days of the month, giving a quick read on consumption and trade.
Power demand and fuel consumption. Electricity demand and diesel sales track industrial and transport activity almost in real time.

body.title: Auto Sales Data: Wholesale vs Retail

columns.label: Wholesale (company and SIAM figures)
points: Vehicles dispatched from factories to dealers
Released early, which is why markets react to it first
Can be inflated by pushing stock onto dealers ahead of festivals or price hikes
Tells you what manufacturers expect to sell

columns.label: Retail (FADA registrations)
points: Vehicles actually registered by customers, based on the government's Vahan database
Shows when dealer inventory is piling up
Tells you what consumers are actually buying

children.text: Financial Market Indicators

Markets are leading indicators too. As Lesson 1.3 showed, the Nifty usually turns before the economy. The shape of the government bond yield curve and the extra yield companies pay over government bonds are also powerful early signals of whether financial conditions are tightening or easing. Lesson 2.2 covers them properly.
Coincident Indicators

Coincident indicators confirm what is happening now. They are less useful for anticipating a turn, but essential for checking whether the signals from your leading indicators are actually showing up in real output.

Index of Industrial Production (IIP). Measures output across mining, manufacturing, and electricity. Released by MoSPI on the 28th of the following month. From June 2026 it uses a new base year of 2022-23.

Index of Core Industries. Tracks key infrastructure industries such as coal, steel, cement, electricity, and refinery products, which carry a large weight in the IIP. Released by DPIIT around the 20th of the following month, so it is an early preview of the IIP. The revised series with base year 2022-23, released in July 2026, adds iron ore as a ninth industry.
GDP. The broadest coincident measure, released quarterly by MoSPI roughly two months after the quarter ends, and now on base year 2022-23.
Lagging Indicators

Lagging indicators move after the cycle has turned. They are poor timing tools, but they are useful for confirming a phase and, crucially, they are what the RBI often reacts to. That makes them a leading indicator of policy, even if they lag the economy.

CPI inflation, especially core inflation (excluding food and fuel). Released by MoSPI on the 12th of the following month. A new series with base year 2024 began in February 2026. Inflation tends to peak late in the cycle and keep falling well into recovery.
Unemployment. MoSPI's Periodic Labour Force Survey has published a monthly bulletin since the April 2025 data, released around the 15th. Companies hire last in a recovery and cut last in a downturn.
Bank gross NPAs. Bad loans surface only after borrowers have been stressed for a while, which is why NPAs peaked in 2018, years after the slowdown began.
Corporate earnings and capacity utilisation. Profits and plant usage respond after demand has already changed, and are published with a lag of weeks to months.

body.text: India rebased almost its entire statistical system in 2026: CPI moved to base year 2024 in February, GDP to 2022-23 in February, IIP to 2022-23 in June, and the Index of Core Industries to 2022-23 in July. New weights, new items, and new methods mean growth rates from the old and new series are not directly comparable. When a year-on-year number looks surprising in 2026 or 2027, check which series it comes from before drawing conclusions.

body.title: Go deeper: four traps that make good data misleading

children.text: Base effects. Year-on-year growth compares with the same month last year. April 2021 growth rates looked spectacular only because April 2020 was a lockdown month. Always ask what the comparison base looked like.

Festival timing. Diwali, Navratri, and Dussehra shift between October and November, so a month can look strong or weak simply because the festive season moved. Compare two-month or festive-season totals instead.

Tax rate changes. GST 2.0, effective 22 September 2025, collapsed most goods into 5% and 18% slabs from the earlier 12% and 28% slabs. Lower rates can reduce collections even when underlying consumption rises, so GST collections before and after that date need careful comparison.
Wholesale vs retail. Factory dispatches can run ahead of real demand for months if dealers are being stuffed with inventory. Cross-check company numbers against FADA retail registrations.
Practice

body.title: Classify the Indicator
body.question: Which of these is best described as a lagging indicator of the business cycle?
options: New orders component of the manufacturing PMI
Gross NPA ratio of scheduled commercial banks
body.explanation: Bad loans surface only after borrowers have been under stress for a long time, so gross NPAs rise well after a slowdown begins and keep falling well into an upcycle. India's NPAs peaked in March 2018, years after the 2011 to 2014 slowdown started. PMI new orders, vehicle dispatches, and the Nifty all tend to move before the broader economy.

body.title: Complete the Rule
body.textWithBlank: A PMI reading above ___ means that more firms reported an improvement than a deterioration compared with the previous month.
body.explanation: Fifty is the dividing line of every PMI. Above 50 signals expansion compared with the previous month, below 50 signals contraction. The distance from 50 indicates how widespread the change is, not its exact size.

body.title: Mixed Signals
body.scenario: Imagine the following readings arrive over one month. Manufacturing PMI has risen from 49 to 53 over the last three months, with new orders at a 12-month high. Company auto dispatches are up 9% year on year, but FADA retail registrations are down 3%. The latest IIP, for two months ago, shows growth of just 1.5%. Core CPI inflation is at a two-year low, and bank gross NPAs are still rising slightly.
body.prompt: What does this dashboard suggest about the phase of the cycle, and which signal would you treat with the most suspicion?
body.modelAnswer: The leading indicators point to an early recovery: the PMI has moved back above 50 and new orders are strengthening. The coincident IIP is still weak, which is normal, because output lags orders and the IIP number is two months old. The lagging indicators fit the same picture: falling core inflation and still-rising NPAs are typical of the tail end of a slowdown. The most suspicious signal is auto sales. Dispatches rising while retail registrations fall suggests manufacturers are pushing inventory to dealers rather than seeing real consumer demand, perhaps ahead of a festive season. The overall read is a tentative early recovery that needs confirmation from retail demand and from the IIP in coming months, not a call to go all in.

body.title: Your Monthly Dashboard Routine
steps: Around the 20th to 25th: note the HSBC India Flash PMI for the current month
1st of the month: check the final manufacturing PMI and company auto sales; compare dispatches with FADA retail data when it arrives
First days of the month: note GST collections, adjusting for the September 2025 GST rate cuts and festival timing
12th: record CPI and core inflation, and note what they imply for the RBI
20th and 28th: check the Index of Core Industries and IIP to see whether PMI signals are showing up in real output
Each quarter: update GDP and bank NPA trends, and label each indicator as improving, stable, or worsening

body.label: S&P Global PMI Releases
body.description: Official press releases for the HSBC India Manufacturing, Services, and Flash PMI, including sub-indices such as new orders and employment.

body.text: This lesson explains economic indicators for educational purposes. It is not investment advice. Indicators can give false or conflicting signals, and release schedules and methodologies can change, so always check the latest official release calendar.

points: Leading indicators turn before the economy, coincident indicators move with it, and lagging indicators confirm a turn after it has happened
The PMI is India's most useful leading indicator: a diffusion index where 50 separates improvement from deterioration, with new orders carrying the largest weight at 30%
In August 2020 the PMI was back above 50 at 52.0, published within days of the record -23.9% GDP print
Cross-check auto dispatches against FADA retail registrations, and adjust GST data for festival timing and the September 2025 rate cuts
IIP (28th), core industries (around the 20th), and GDP are coincident; CPI (12th), unemployment, NPAs, and earnings are lagging
India rebased GDP, CPI, IIP, and core industries in 2026, so old and new growth rates are not directly comparable
Read the dashboard in sequence: leading signals first, then check whether coincident data confirms them
